extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/graduate students and researchers in enumerative combinatorics and discrete mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook section presenting definitions, bijections, enumerative results, and generating-function identities for permutations, increasing trees, alternating permutations (Euler numbers), min-max trees and the cd-index, permutations of multisets (q-multinomial identities), and partition identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection T(w) between permutations and increasing binary trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Define T(w) for a word w on distinct letters by taking the least element i of w as the root, factoring w = u i v, letting T(u) and T(v) be the left and right subtrees of i, inductively. The permutation w is recovered from T(w) by reading labels in symmetric (inorder) order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction yields a bijection between Sn and increasing binary trees on n vertices (labels 1..n) such that labels along any root-to-leaf path are increasing. See Figure 1.7 and example T(57316284) in Figure 1.8. Left/right successors of a vertex correspond to least elements to left/right in w with all intermediate elements > that vertex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element types <-> vertex successor correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify element wi of permutation w as double rise (wi-1 < wi < wi+1), double fall (wi-1 > wi > wi+1), peak (wi-1 < wi > wi+1), or valley (wi-1 > wi < wi+1) (with w0 = wn+1 = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These element types correspond to vertex successor counts in T(w): double rise ↔ precisely a right successor; double fall ↔ precisely a left successor; valley ↔ left and right successors; peak ↔ no successors. This correspondence allows properties of permutations to be read off trees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count of increasing binary trees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of increasing binary trees with n vertices is n! (Proposition 1.5.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from bijection T(w) with permutations in Sn; each permutation gives a unique increasing binary tree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eulerian numbers count left-successor statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of increasing binary trees on n vertices for which exactly k vertices have left successors is the Eulerian number A(n, k+1) (Proposition 1.5.3(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distribution of left-successor counts corresponds to descent statistics of permutations via the T(w) bijection; see Proposition 1.3.1 referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete increasing binary trees ↔ alternating permutations
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of complete (every vertex either an endpoint or has two successors) increasing binary trees with 2n+1 vertices equals E_{2n+1}, the number of alternating permutations in S_{2n+1} (Proposition 1.5.3(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects tree completeness to alternating permutation enumerations (Euler numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection T'(w) to unordered increasing trees (root 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given w = w1...wn, define unordered tree T'(w) on vertices 0,1,...,n by making i the successor of the rightmost element j < i that precedes i in w; if none exists, i is successor of root 0. This gives a bijection between Sn and increasing (unordered) trees on n+1 vertices (Section 1.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successors of 0 are left-to-right minima of w; endpoints correspond to elements wi with i=1 or wi < all previous elements. Example: T'(57316284) in Figure 1.9. Use this to translate permutation statistics to unordered trees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count of unordered increasing trees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of unordered increasing trees on n+1 vertices is n! (Proposition 1.5.5(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from bijection T'(w) with permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root-successor distribution via signless Stirling numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of unordered increasing trees on n+1 vertices for which the root has k successors equals the signless Stirling number c(n, k) (Proposition 1.5.5(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects tree root-degree distribution to cycle-type enumerations (Stirling numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Endpoint counts via Eulerian numbers for unordered trees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of unordered increasing trees on n+1 vertices with k endpoints is the Eulerian number A(n, k) (Proposition 1.5.5(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Again translates permutation descent/ascents statistics to tree endpoint counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternating permutations generating function: sec x + tan x
rubrics_metrics.description: The exponential generating function for Euler numbers En (number of alternating permutations in Sn with E0 = 1) is sum_{n≥0} E_n x^n/n! = sec x + tan x (Proposition 1.6.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads to parity separation: sum_{n≥0} E_{2n} x^{2n}/(2n)! = sec x and sum_{n≥0} E_{2n+1} x^{2n+1}/(2n+1)! = tan x. Series coefficients given: 1,1,1,2,5,16,61,...

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence and differential equation for Euler numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Combinatorial decomposition yields 2E_{n+1} = sum_{k=0}^n binom(n,k) E_k E_{n-k} (equation (1.55)), which translates to differential equation 2y' = y^2 + 1 with y(0)=1, giving y = sec x + tan x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate recurrence by considering position of 1 in alternating permutations; also gives other recurrences and combinatorial proofs (Exercises referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization fk(n) for descent set multiples of k
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f_k(n) be number of permutations in S_{kn} with descent set {k,2k,3k,...}. Then generating-function identity: sum_{n≥0} f_k(kn) x^{kn}/(kn)! = sum_{n≥0} (-1)^n x^{kn}/(kn)! (equations (1.58)-(1.59)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes the alternating-permutation/secant-tangent phenomenon and invites more conceptual proofs (Section 3.19, Inclusion-Exclusion for k=2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flip equivalence of increasing binary trees
rubrics_metrics.description: Define flip at vertex v as interchanging left and right subtrees. Two increasing binary trees are equivalent if reachable by a sequence of flips. The number of increasing binary trees equivalent to T is 2^{n-ε(T)}, where ε(T) is number of endpoints (Section 1.6.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence classes correspond to increasing (1,2)-trees (unordered children), and orbits under the elementary flips generate a group isomorphic to (Z/2Z)^n acting on Tn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of increasing (1,2)-trees equals Euler numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f(n) be number of increasing (1,2)-trees on vertex set [n]; then f(n) = E_n (Proposition 1.6.2). The generating function y = sum f(n+1) x^n/n! satisfies y' = 1 + y + (1/2) y^2 with y(0)=0, whose unique solution is sec x + tan x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinatorial decomposition: root has 0,1 or 2 subtrees; symmetric ordering when two subtrees so factor 1/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Min-max tree M(w) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For sequence w = a1...an of distinct integers, define M(w) as binary tree with root the earliest position j that is either the minimum or maximum of the whole sequence; left subtree is M(a1...a_{j-1}), right subtree M(a_{j+1}...a_n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: no vertex has only a left successor; each vertex is min or max of its subtree. Example in Figure 1.11(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operators ψ_i on min-max trees (commuting involutions & group)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each position i define involution ψ_i that permutes labels in the subtree Mai consisting of node ai and its right subtree: if ai is min replace it by largest of Mai and reorder remaining elements keeping relative order, and dually if ai is max. The ψ_i's commute and generate a group G_w ≅ (Z/2Z)^{ι(w)} where ι(w) is number of internal vertices (Fact #1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those ψ_i for which ai is not an endpoint form a minimal generating set. Each ψ acts only on labels inside Mai; examples shown in Figures 1.11(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of ψ_i on descent sets (local rules)
rubrics_metrics.description:
If ai is an internal vertex with only a right child then D(ψ_i w) = D(w) ∪ {i} 
ot	ext{?} (and symmetric rules). If ai has both children then exactly one of i,i+1 belongs to D(w) and D(ψ_i w) is obtained by toggling membership of i and possibly i-1 according to explicit formulas (Fact #2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The changes in descent sets for different i occur independently (equivalent to commutativity), enabling encoding of class descent-sets by noncommutative polynomials; see examples and Fact #2 for precise formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic monomial u_S and ab-index Ψ_n
rubrics_metrics.description: For S ⊆ [n-1] define characteristic monomial u_S = e_1 e_2 ... e_{n-1} with e_i = a if i∉S and b if i∈S. Define Ψ_n = sum_{w∈S_n} u_{D(w)} = sum_{S⊆[n-1]} β(S) u_S (equation (1.63)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ψ_n is the ab-index of the symmetric group (or boolean algebra B_n). Example: Ψ_3 = aa + 2ab + 2ba + bb.

rubrics_metrics.name: cd-index: Ψ_n expressed in c=a+b and d=ab+ba
rubrics_metrics.description: The ab-index Ψ_n can be written as a polynomial Φ_n in noncommutative variables c=a+b and d=ab+ba; this cd-index Φ_n is a sum of E_n monomials (Theorem 1.6.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Φ_n is more compact than Ψ_n: number of distinct cd-terms is Fibonacci F_n vs 2^{n-1} ab-terms. Examples for small n given: Φ_3 = c^2 + d, Φ_4 = c^3 + 2c d + 2 d c, etc. This representation groups contributions of M-equivalence classes via Φ_w(c,d)=Φ_w'(c,d,1) and identity (1.62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequalities among β_n(S) via ω(S) and cd-index positivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ω(S) ⊆ [n-2] by membership rule (i ∈ ω(S) iff exactly one of i,i+1 is in S). If ω(S) ⊆ ω(T) then β_n(S) < β_n(T) (Proposition 1.6.4). Corollary: among all S with ω(S) ⊆ [set], maxima/minima determined by alternating or reverse-alternating pattern (Corollary 1.6.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses that Φ_n has nonnegative coefficients and that grouping by M-equivalence classes yields sums Φ_w(a+b,ab+ba) = sum_{v∈[w]} u_{D(v)} (Fact #3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutations of multisets: descent set and inv generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: For a multiset M (finite, totally ordered underlying set) define permutations w of M, descent set D(w) = {i : w_i > w_{i+1}}, number of descents des(w), major index maj(w) and inversions inv(w) as pairs (i,j) with i<j and w_i > w_j, counting positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All standard permutation statistics extend to multisets but with care: an inversion must include positions not just values (because repeated values may occur). Definitions set up q-analog enumerations for multiset permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-multinomial identity for permutations of a multiset
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiset M with multiplicities a1,...,am summing to n, sum_{w∈S_M} q^{inv(w)} = [n; a1,...,am]_q (the q-multinomial coefficient) (Proposition 1.7.1, equation (1.68)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs provided: a semi-combinatorial proof via recurrences (1.69)-(1.70) reducing to Q(n,k) and a bijective proof using a block-concatenation map φ relating multiset permutations to sequences of permutations. Specialization q=1 recovers ordinary multinomial coefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-binomial count of k-dimensional subspaces of F_q^n
rubrics_metrics.description: The number G(n,k) of k-dimensional subspaces of F_q^n equals the Gaussian/binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q = (q^n-1)...(q^{n-k+1}-1)/((q^k-1)...(q-1)) (Proposition 1.7.2, equation (1.72)-(1.73)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof counts ordered independent k-tuples versus selecting subspace then basis; q-analogue of n!/(k!(n-k)!). This identity is used to combinatorially interpret q-binomial coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: q-binomial equals generating function for partitions in j×k box
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix j,k∈N. Then sum_{n≥0} p(j,k,n) q^n = [j+k choose j]_q, where p(j,k,n) is number of partitions of n into at most k parts with largest part ≤ j (Proposition 1.7.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combinatorial proof via row-reduced echelon matrices over F_q: parameters a_i (first pivot column indices) map to partition parts λ_i = a_i + i - (something) and counting free parameters gives q^{|λ|}. Also remark that this is the cellular decomposition of the Grassmannian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection: partitions in rectangle ↔ multiset permutations with given inversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given partition λ fitting in j×k rectangle, encode its Young diagram boundary as lattice path from top-right to bottom-left; write 1 for horizontal step and 2 for vertical step to obtain permutation w of multiset with a specified number of inversions equal to |λ| (construction in Section 1.7 leading to Proposition 1.7.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions of 2's are at indices j+λ_i + i; example λ=(4,3,1) in a 5×3 rectangle yields the word shown in Figure 1.15. This gives a bijective combinatorial proof that q^{|λ|} terms correspond to permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition generating-function product formulas (bounded and unbounded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generating function for partitions with largest part ≤ k: sum_{n≥0} p_{≤k}(n) q^n = product_{i=1}^k 1/(1-q^i) (equation (1.76)). Taking k→∞ gives sum_{n≥0} p(n) q^n = product_{i≥1} 1/(1-q^i) (equation (1.77)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation interprets partitions as solutions m1 + 2m2 + ... + k m_k = n with m_i ≥ 0 and factors the generating function as geometric series in each q^i; standard and fundamental partition generating-function identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: General restricted-partition generating function (S_i constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P(S) be set of partitions λ such that multiplicity m_i(λ) ∈ S_i for each i (with S_i ⊆ N given). Then generating function F(S,q) = sum_{λ∈P(S)} q^{|λ|} = product_{i≥1} (sum_{j∈S_i} q^{i j}) (Proposition 1.8.1, equation (1.78)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialize by taking S_i finite/sets to obtain many classical generating functions; corollary recovers counting p(S,n) by setting all q_i = q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition identity: sum_{i≥1} (i-1) λ_i = sum_{i≥1} binom(λ'_i,2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any partition λ with conjugate λ', identity holds: sum_i (i-1) λ_i = sum_i binom(λ'_i,2) (Proposition 1.8.3, equation (1.79)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via filling Young diagram square (i-1) in each square of row i and summing by rows vs by columns; combinatorial/diagrammatic equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating function for self-conjugate partitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let c(n) be number of self-conjugate partitions of n. Then sum_{n≥0} c(n) q^n = product_{k≥0} (1 + q^{2k+1}) = (1+q)(1+q^3)(1+q^5)... (Proposition 1.8.4, equation (1.80)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses description of self-conjugate partitions via diagonal hooks (Figure 1.16): each diagonal hook contributes an odd-length part and choices are independent, giving factor (1+q^{odd}).
